rejected_findings.title: New comment asserts closes_at is NOT NULL, but the replaced predicate explicitly guarded IS NOT NULL — one of them is wrong
rejected_findings.rejection_reason: vacancy.closes_at is TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL (supabase/migrations/00000000000001_initial_schema.sql:54). The new comment is correct; the old IS NOT NULL guard was dead code. Blind lens cannot see the schema by design.

rejected_findings.title: Continue-draft email still frames the expiry promise as 'the vacancy close' while retention now keeps drafts 7 days beyond it
rejected_findings.rejection_reason: The email body (email_client.gleam:580-583) promises link functionality ('This link works until the vacancy closes'), which stays literally true — the link renders the closed page once closed; grace changes draft retention, never link availability. No deletion-timing disclosure exists in the email, so no storage-limitation breach. The deletion-timing copy (draft_view.gleam erasure confirm) WAS updated.

findings.title: Re-close grace pin test never stamps closed_notified_at, so it passes even if extend_vacancy drops the NULL-clear it claims to guard
findings.evidence: auto_close_with_closes_at (lines 586-594) sets only 'status = \'closed\', closed_via = \'auto\', closes_at = now() - interval ...' — never closed_notified_at; seed_vacancy leaves the stamp NULL; the post-extend assertion 'SELECT COALESCE(closed_notified_at::text, \'\') ... should.equal(Ok(\'\'))' (line 765) therefore passes vacuously.
findings.detail: extend_vacancy.sql:41 today clears closed_notified_at = NULL (verified), but every assertion in this test passes with that clear dropped: the stamp is NULL from seed throughout. In production auto-closed rows DO get stamped (mark_vacancy_close_notified.sql), so the stale-stamp scenario the doc comment describes is real — and no test would catch a regression that drops the clear. The test's comment ('If a future edit drops that NULL-clear, this test fails') overclaims; the PR body's 'Review pass' section repeats the claim.
findings.recommended_fix: Stamp closed_notified_at explicitly in the first close (close_vacancy_manual or a direct UPDATE) old enough to exceed 7 days at the second sweep; seed the draft after the first sweep so a stale stamp would actually delete it.

findings.title: Active-but-expired vacancy (status not 'closed', closes_at past) lost its draft-sweep pin in the test rewrite — documented lifecycle-outage edge untested
findings.evidence: Removed by the diff: '// Still-active status but closes_at already passed (auto-close window)… let assert Ok(past_id) = test_db.seed_vacancy(db, landlord_id, True)'. Both new helpers force status='closed' ('SET status = \'closed\', closed_via = \'auto\',' line 590). The SQL comment documents the untested state: 'Edge, accepted: a vacancy that sits active-but-expired for >7 days (lifecycle job down AND no landlord dashboard visit...) loses its drafts'.
findings.detail: The old suite pinned deletion for a still-active vacancy with closes_at past; the rewrite exercises the status-agnostic time-based branch only with status='closed' rows. Neither the in-grace survival (active, closes_at 3d past) nor the documented >7d-outage deletion of an active-but-expired vacancy is pinned. A future edit adding a status condition to the time-based branch would ship green.
findings.recommended_fix: Add two cases: vacancy left status='active' with closes_at 3d past (draft survives) and 8d past (draft swept via the time-based branch).

findings.title: RunSummary.application_drafts_expired field doc still preaches the pre-amendment 'drafts die at vacancy close' semantic
findings.detail: The diff updated the sweep_application_drafts comment ~200 lines below in the same file ('Drafts die 7 days AFTER vacancy close (draft-grace-period amendment)') and both SQL comments, but missed this field doc, which still states the old close-time deletion semantic.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword to match the amendment, e.g. 'vacancy close older than the 7-day extension grace (draft-grace-period amendment)'.

findings.title: Exact 7-day grace threshold unpinned — any constant in (3d, 8d] passes the new tests
findings.evidence: Predicate: '<= now() - interval \'7 days\'' (both branches). Test offsets are exclusively 1/3/8 days: 'close_vacancy_manual(db, manual_recent_id, "3 days")', '"8 days"', 'auto_close_with_closes_at(db, time_recent_id, "3 days")', '"8 days"'.
findings.detail: Factually true: a regression of the constant to 4-8 days satisfies every assertion. Demoted to note: the briefing's acceptance criteria literally specified the 3d/8d brackets, and the daily sweep cadence already makes the effective boundary fuzzy (a draft 7d0h vs 7d23h past close is swept on the same daily run).
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: bracket the threshold (e.g. closes_at 6 days 23 hours past survives, 7 days 1 hour past deleted) for at least one branch.

findings.title: Documented archived-and-long-expired sweep behavior has no test pin
findings.evidence: seed_archived_vacancy inserts 'NOW() + INTERVAL \'30 days\'' for closes_at; the only archived assertion is survival ('draft_field(db, archived_id, "continue_token") |> should.equal("tok-archived")'). The new SQL comment documents: 'the time-based branch still sweeps an archived-and-long-expired vacancy\'s drafts'.
findings.detail: The amended SQL comment newly documents that an archived vacancy with closes_at >7d past still loses drafts, but no test pins archived+expired deletion. Pre-existing behavior, disclosed in the PR body as deliberately unchanged.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one case: archived vacancy with closes_at 8 days past and a seeded draft; assert the sweep deletes it.
